Empirical Research Plan  
“Climate Adaptation and Agricultural Productivity in U.S. Counties, 1950-2015”

====================================================================
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Principal design: Staggered Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event-study
extension.

Why DID?  
•  We observe the same counties repeatedly for >60 years, during which the
   intensity of climate change (especially extreme heat) rises in some places
   earlier and more strongly than in others.  
•  Counties that have not yet experienced a large climate shift in a given year
   provide a natural counterfactual for counties that already have.  
•  The design permits flexible dynamics (event study) to measure (i) how
   quickly farmers adapt after a substantial climate shift and (ii) the net
   effect of that adaptation on yields.

We will implement the modern «interaction-weighted» DID estimators of
Callaway & Sant’Anna (2021) / Sun & Abraham (2021) to account for staggered
treatment timing.

====================================================================
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
•  Compute, for every county c and calendar year t, the 5-year moving‐average
   of «Harmful Degree Days» (HDD)—­temperatures >30 °C during the growing
   season.  
•  Define the county-specific “treatment year” G_c as the first year the
   5-year mean HDD exceeds its own 1950-1969 mean by ≥1.5 standard deviations.  
•  Treated observations: all county-years τ ≥ G_c.  
•  Untreated observations: county-years before G_c as well as counties that
   never cross the threshold by 2015 (never-treated).

Interpretation: treatment = the onset of a materially hotter climate to which
farmers must adapt.

Control group  
•  In each calendar year, the control group consists of counties that have not
   yet crossed the threshold (plus never-treated in all years). This follows
   the “not-yet-treated” logic of staggered DID.

Outcome variables  
(1) Crop yields (bushels/acre) for corn and soy.  
(2) Adaptation proxies: share of acres irrigated, adoption of heat-tolerant
    seed, shifts in planting dates, crop switching indicators.  

Timing/Event window  
We code event time k = t − G_c where k∈[−10,…,+20]. We will estimate
y_{c,t} = Σ_{k≠−1} β_k · 1{k=k} + γ_c + δ_t + X_{c,t}θ + ε_{c,t},
with k = −1 omitted.

====================================================================
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of a large climate shift, treated and
     control counties’ yields would have evolved similarly.  
     – Plausibility: Neighboring counties often cross the HDD threshold in
       different years, and we include state-by-year fixed effects plus rich
       pre-trends tests.

A2. No anticipation: Farmers cannot perfectly predict the exact calendar year
     their county will cross the HDD threshold.  
     – Plausibility: Threshold is defined on a 5-year moving average of weather
       realizations, which remain partly stochastic.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (no spatial spillovers): A county crossing the
     threshold does not directly change the weather or market conditions in
     control counties.  
     – Plausibility: Weather is exogenous; however commodity prices are partly
       national, so we include year fixed effects to net out common shocks.

A4. Composition: County borders and agricultural activity remain intact; no
     massive re-definition of counties.  
     – Plausibility: U.S. county boundaries are largely fixed over the period.

====================================================================
4. Main Threats & Mitigation
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Differential technological progress  
    •  Precision ag and GMO seeds diffused faster in hotter regions.  
    •  Mitigation: control for county-level patent counts, extension service
      presence, and include region-specific time trends.

T2. Economic confounders (e.g., farm subsidies, ethanol demand)  
    •  Mitigation: include crop-specific policy controls (e.g., CRP acreage,
      subsidy rates) and national commodity-price × crop fixed effects.

T3. Measurement error in HDD and yields  
    •  Weather data gridded to counties may be noisy.  
    •  Mitigation: aggregate to 3-year bins as robustness; instrument HDD with
      upper-air reanalysis temperatures; drop counties with <90 % weather-
      station coverage.

====================================================================
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
############################################################
# 0. Packages
############################################################
library(data.table)   # fast I/O
library(fixest)       # high-dim FE regressions
library(did)          # Callaway-Sant’Anna estimator
library(ggplot2)

############################################################
# 1. Load and merge data
############################################################
ag   <- fread("county_crop_yields.csv")      # yield data
wx   <- fread("county_weather.csv")          # daily/max temp, precip
prct <- fread("county_practices.csv")        # irrigation, seeds, etc.

# Merge
setkey(ag, fips, year)
setkey(wx, fips, year)
setkey(prct, fips, year)
dat <- merge(ag, wx, all=TRUE)
dat <- merge(dat, prct, all=TRUE)

############################################################
# 2. Variable construction
############################################################
# Harmful Degree Days (growing season Apr–Sep)
dat[, HDD := pmax(temp_max - 30, 0)]   # daily then annualize earlier
# 5-year moving average
setorder(dat, fips, year)
dat[, HDD_ma := frollmean(HDD, n = 5, align = "right"), by = fips]

# Baseline mean & SD 1950-1969
base <- dat[year %between% c(1950, 1969),
            .(HDD_base = mean(HDD_ma, na.rm=TRUE),
              SD_base  = sd(HDD_ma,   na.rm=TRUE)),
            by = fips]
dat  <- merge(dat, base, by="fips")
dat[, treated := (HDD_ma - HDD_base) / SD_base >= 1.5 ]

# First treatment year G_c
dat[, G := ifelse(any(treated==TRUE),
                  min(year[treated==TRUE]), NA), by=fips]

# Event time k
dat[, k := year - G]

############################################################
# 3. Callaway-Sant’Anna DID
############################################################
cs_res <- att_gt(yname   = "corn_yield",
                 gname   = "G",
                 idname  = "fips",
                 tname   = "year",
                 xformla = ~ irrigation_share + precip_tot,
                 data    = dat,
                 control_group = "notyettreated")

# Aggregate to dynamic effects
dyn <- aggte(cs_res, type = "dynamic")
summary(dyn)
ggplot(data=dyn$egt, aes(x=event.time, y=att.egt)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, linetype="dashed") +
  theme_minimal()

############################################################
# 4. Two-way FE (robustness)
############################################################
fe_res <- feols(corn_yield ~ treated + irrigation_share + precip_tot |
                  fips + year,
                data = dat)
summary(fe_res)

############################################################
# 5. Placebo test: fake threshold at 0.5 SD
############################################################
dat[, treated_placebo := (HDD_ma - HDD_base)/SD_base >= 0.5 ]
fe_placebo <- feols(corn_yield ~ treated_placebo |
                      fips + year, data = dat[year < G-5])
summary(fe_placebo)
```

====================================================================
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Prior: A sudden, sustained rise in extreme heat initially lowers yields (β₀ < 0),
but the negative effect attenuates within ~10 years as farmers adopt irrigation,
heat-tolerant hybrids, and adjust planting dates.  
Magnitude: Immediate impact −8 % (≈−12 bu/acre for corn) in first 3 years;
converging to −2 % (≈−3 bu/acre) after a decade.

====================================================================
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
(C1) Parallel pre-trends visually and statistically supported .............. 1  
(C2) Correctly addresses staggered timing (modern estimator) ............... 1  
(C3) No anticipation / no manipulation of crossing year ................... 0.5  
(C4) No spillovers between counties ....................................... 0.5  
(C5) Robustness to alternative thresholds & placebo tests ................. 1  
Total (out of 5) .......................................................... 4  

====================================================================
This plan leverages rich spatial-temporal variation in U.S. weather to credibly
trace both the short-run damage from climate shocks and the longer-run
productivity gains from farmers’ adaptive responses.
